commentary: The market is in a strong AI and chip rally, and every name we track is up big over the past few months. When everything has already run this hard, the job is to be picky rather than to chase. We are putting real money into just one name today - Dell - because it is the rare stock that has ridden the AI-server boom while still trading at a sensible price, and it recently paused rather than spiking straight up, which gives us a cleaner place to buy. The collapse of rival Super Micro is actually helping Dell, as customers move their orders to a more reliable supplier. We are watching inflation, which is creeping back up and could eventually spook the most expensive tech stocks - another reason we chose the cheaper, steadier option. We would change our mind and sell if AI-server demand shows cracks or the stock falls back below its recent trend.

watchlist.one_line: Best-in-class AI accelerator momentum with a fresh, concrete catalyst - we just want a better entry.
watchlist.thoughts: AMD jumped 5.7% today on a major AI infrastructure alliance, and Goldman sees it entering its Aug 4 earnings with a server-CPU advantage. Revenue and gross profit are inflecting hard (Q1 revenue $7.4B, gross profit $3.7B). The setup and story are excellent. What stops us is price and timing: chasing a 5.7% pop directly into an earnings binary two weeks out is poor swing discipline. We would buy on a pullback toward the 20-day area or after digesting the earnings reaction.
watchlist.would_buy_at: On a pullback toward ~500-510, or after the 8/4 earnings print if the reaction is constructive

watchlist.one_line: High-quality AI networking compounder with accelerating momentum, but no margin of safety at the current price.
watchlist.thoughts: Arista is a premier data-center networking name (revenue $2.0B, net income $814M in Q1, ~40% net margin) with +18% one-month momentum and a strong Broadcom-partner/Nvidia-rival narrative drawing fresh analyst attention. The problem for a swing entry is that it sits just 2.7% below its 52-week high with no pullback at all, at a rich ~41x forward multiple - buying strength here means paying up with little cushion. We want either a pullback to buy into or an earnings-driven breakout to confirm.
watchlist.would_buy_at: Near ~170 on a pullback, or on a confirmed breakout after 8/4 earnings

watchlist.one_line: Analog-cycle recovery with real 3-month momentum, but an earnings binary sits right inside the swing window.
watchlist.thoughts: Texas Instruments has re-rated (+48% 3m) on an analog-demand recovery and heavy US-fab capex, and it pulled back a healthy 7.6% from its 20-day high - a decent entry structurally. The blocker is timing: earnings on 7/22 is only 13 days out, an event I do not want to underwrite blind mid-swing. We would rather see the print, then buy the reaction if the analog recovery and 2026 guidance confirm.
watchlist.would_buy_at: After 7/22 earnings, on a constructive reaction and guidance

watchlist.one_line: The cheapest AI-server share-gain beneficiary in the group, waiting on momentum to re-engage.
watchlist.thoughts: HPE is the deep-value way to play the same Super Micro share-shift thesis as Dell, at a strikingly low ~12.3x forward P/E and 1.7x sales, and it popped ~10% today. But its one-month momentum is actually negative (-1.2%) and it remains 23% below its 52-week high, so the trend is not yet confirmed the way Dell's is. We prefer Dell for now but would rotate attention to HPE if it reclaims its recent highs on volume.
watchlist.would_buy_at: On a reclaim of the recent breakdown level with follow-through, near ~50-52

watchlist.one_line: Explosive connectivity growth story, too volatile to size cleanly at today's price.
watchlist.thoughts: Credo is up 165% in a year on AI-connectivity (AEC/optical) demand and has a compelling forward multiple (~30x) relative to its growth. The obstacle is risk control: an 11%+ ATR and a 13.9% drawdown from its 20-day high make a sensible stop hard to place without either getting shaken out or risking too much. We would want it to stabilize and build a tighter base before committing capital.
watchlist.would_buy_at: After it bases and tightens, on a pullback toward ~240-250

macro_regime_hint.label: supportive
macro_regime_hint.note: Deterministic hint only — the agent must form its own regime view.

proposal.thesis: Dell is the best risk/reward in an extended AI-server complex: it pairs elite momentum (+143% 3m, +202% 6m) with the cheapest valuation in the group (forward P/E ~20.9, P/S 2.2) and a constructive entry, having pulled back only 2.2% from its 20-day high while sitting 4.1% off its 52-week high near a buy point. The 29% collapse in Super Micro is a direct tailwind, consolidating enterprise/AI-server share toward Dell as customers de-risk suppliers. Q1 fundamentals (revenue $23.4B, net income $965M) confirm profitable scale, and the current tape ('Dell Stock Nears Buy Point') shows institutional demand building. With no earnings until 9/3, a 45-day swing captures the momentum leg without event risk.
catalysts: Breakout through the buy point on sustained AI-server order momentum over the next 2-4 weeks
Continued Super Micro share-shift narrative benefiting Dell (ongoing, July 2026)
Positive pre-announcement/analyst upgrades ahead of the Sept 3 earnings print
proposal.macro_context: Regime is supportive for AI/data-center longs: falling Fed funds, tight credit spreads, low VIX (16.9) and easy financial conditions, with the tape confirming a chip/AI-led Nasdaq rally. The one caveat is re-accelerating CPI (4.27%) and rising long rates (10Y 4.56%), which pressure the highest-multiple names most - precisely why Dell's ~21x forward multiple is the right way to express this trade rather than a 40-100x momentum name.
proposal.risk_map: The trade breaks if AI-server demand cools or gross-margin fears (the Super Micro overhang) spread to Dell - watched via any negative pre-announcement, channel checks, or a close back below the 50-DMA. A broader chip/AI momentum unwind driven by the rising-rate/sticky-inflation backdrop would also hit it; the 408 stop (-9.4% from last close, within ATR) caps the loss and exits before the thesis fully unwinds.

improvements.note: Every top candidate now carries forward revenue-growth and 30-day analyst EPS-revision data. The agent asked for this so it can judge whether a stock's valuation is deserved using hard estimate trends instead of news tone. First readout: Dell shows 50.8 percent forward revenue growth with estimates being revised up.

** The context bundle gives me valuation and price/momentum but no consensus estimates or forward revenue-growth figures, so I'm forced to lean on trailing fundamentals plus headline sentiment when judging whether a rich multiple (ANET at 41x, ALAB at 97x) is justified. Adding forward revenue-growth and EPS-revision (analyst estimate trend) fields per candidate would materially sharpen the "is this multiple deserved" call and reduce reliance on qualitative news vibes — the single biggest lever on proposal quality this run.

** The context bundle deep-researches only the top-5 by deterministic score, but two of those five (TXN, AMD) are effectively un-actionable this run because of earnings timing (7/22) or a same-day news gap — meaning I burned my richest data (filings, 13F, news) on names I won't trade, while candidates like HPE and CRDO that I'm actively weighing had only a price and momentum row. Adding a `next_earnings` field and a `days_to_earnings` flag directly into the `universe_scan.top_setups` rows (not just the news block), plus expanding SEC/news enrichment to the top 8 rather than top 5, would let me screen out earnings-binary setups before spending research budget and give me fundamentals on the names I actually end up considering.

** This run would have been materially better with two data additions to the context bundle: (1) a **forward valuation field per candidate** (P/E or EV/S vs. its own 1-yr history) — right now I'm inferring "extended" purely from price momentum, when the real question for the CPI/rate-driven multiple-compression thesis is whether valuations are stretched, and (2) **intraday/1-day price change** so I can distinguish a name resting after a run from one spiking on news *today* (AMD) without cross-referencing headline timestamps by hand. Adding a `pct_change_1d` to the price block and a `valuation` sub-object to each `top_setups` entry would sharpen entry-timing judgment on exactly the chase-vs-wait decisions that dominated this cycle.
